headline: High risk of data leakage and cascading errors: RD-Agent’s broad API/file access can expose artifacts and logs while Argo Workflows can propagate them into automated workflows.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared channel is documented, so direct prompt injection is not established. However, Argo Workflows can pass artifacts/parameters and RD-Agent reads/writes logs and files, so if an operator bridges them via files or copied outputs, malicious content could be reinterpreted. The pathway is indirect and requires unusual setup.
conditions: IF an operator copies RD-Agent logs or artifacts into Argo parameters or files, injection becomes possible.
IF a shared filesystem or message queue is introduced between the agents, injection risk increases.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Disable any manual copy-paste of model outputs into workflow inputs.
Add a review step before Argo consumes RD-Agent-generated text.
Use strict file schemas for any exchanged artifacts.

B_data_leakage.rationale: RD-Agent handles secrets and broad external APIs, while Argo Workflows touches artifacts and parameters and can egress to allowlisted networks. If they share a workspace or operator-managed files, sensitive research data or credentials can flow from one into the other’s outputs or API calls. The interaction is plausible in default-style automation, though not directly documented.
conditions: IF both agents read from the same directory or artifact store, leakage becomes plausible.
IF RD-Agent secrets are present in files that Argo can ingest, those secrets may be exposed downstream.
mitigations: Store secrets outside shared directories.
Separate artifact and log locations per agent.
Redact credentials before any handoff.
Restrict Argo inputs to whitelisted file types.
requires-engineering: add provenance-aware access controls.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Argo Workflows can write workflow artifacts and call APIs, while RD-Agent supports multiple instances and broad API use. If both are pointed at the same mutable workspace or external resource, concurrent writes or conflicting API actions can occur. The profiles do not show locking or coordination, so uncertainty pushes this to medium.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory, git repo, or dataset, conflicts can occur.
IF both agents target the same external API credentials or mutable resource, race conditions are possible.
mitigations: Assign separate output directories.
Serialize writes with a simple lock file.
Use distinct API credentials per agent.
Run one agent at a time for shared resources.
requires-engineering: add transactional coordination.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Argo Workflows can operationalize artifacts and parameters, and RD-Agent produces research outputs, logs, and traces that may be treated as authoritative. If Argo consumes RD-Agent output without verification, incorrect facts can cascade into automated workflow actions. Because the downstream blast radius can affect multiple work products or actions, high is warranted.
conditions: IF Argo uses RD-Agent outputs as workflow parameters without validation, errors can cascade.
IF RD-Agent-generated logs or traces are promoted to decision inputs, downstream actions may be wrong.
mitigations: Insert a human review gate before execution.
Validate outputs against a schema.
Require source citations for any factual claims.
Limit Argo to read-only consumption of RD-Agent outputs.
requires-engineering: add automated consistency checks.

E_compliance.rationale: RD-Agent explicitly handles financial reports, competition datasets, and API keys, while Argo Workflows touches artifacts and parameters and can egress to allowlisted networks. If regulated or sensitive data is routed through Argo without matching retention or residency controls, compliance gaps can arise. The profiles do not document matching controls, so medium is the safest choice.
conditions: IF regulated datasets or financial reports are passed through shared workflow artifacts, compliance obligations may be triggered.
IF retention or deletion policies differ between the two systems, records may persist longer than intended.
mitigations: Classify data before handoff.
Avoid routing regulated data through shared artifacts.
Set explicit retention windows for logs and outputs.
Review residency requirements for any external API calls.
requires-engineering: implement policy-based data handling.
